title: Which Maker has the most robust eventing system?

posts.author: Sasakiken
posts.body:
Hello all,
Despite all the bells and whistles of the newer maker series I find myself preferring to event actions in the game rather than look for plug ins, this might sound a bit archaic.
While scouring old forum posts I saw a lot of discussion on the power of rpg maker 2000/2003's eventing system, more so 2003 which was used to make yume nikki.
I picked up 2003 a while ago and wonder how the eventing system compares to MV which I also own or MZ which I plan to get.
Is 2003 more powerful than the modern makers event wise?

posts.author: ShadowDragon
posts.body:
so far I know, eventing may be equal in each maker.
however, if scriptcalls comes to play, it should be looked how they are used.
MV and MZ are mostly the same with minor changes (depends on the target).
but it also depends what kind of complex eventing you do.
I used XP and VXAce (as I own them) as well for MV.
as MV and MZ used JavaScript, its easier to work with.
I don't know ruby and know it very little from Trihan's tutorial thread.
so you can if you ask me, go for MV or MZ =)

posts.body: Thank you, I got MV but I was just curious :3

posts.author: caethyril
posts.body:
Event commands in 2k3 are mostly more powerful, due to having more built-in options, e.g.
Picture settings: Z layer, pin to map/screen, variable-named images, animation, etc.
Reference by variable ID, e.g. if var 1 = 5, variable ID {var 1} returns the value of var 5.
Show Text: show face on right and/or flipped, allow event movement during text, etc.
Various screen transition options (hide/show screen, map transfers, battle start/end).
2 Timers, in case you need that.
However, newer makers like MV can more than make up for this by using script calls and/or plugins.
In case you want to try it, I think the free trial version of MZ here is still available?
RPG Maker MZ | RPG Maker | Make Your Own Video Games!
Introducing RPG Maker MZ, the latest version from the RPG Maker series that allows anyone to make an RPG with ease! Thanks to new functions and improved operations, on top of accessing an enhanced creative environment and more powerful production elements, you can make a game that really answers...
www.rpgmakerweb.com
For event commands, MV and MZ are almost the same; any gaps can be bridged using script calls and/or plugins. I think the main benefit of MZ over MV is the design of its core scripts, e.g. MZ games make better use of the GPU. MZ also supports 3D particle animations (Effekseer) out of the box,
in addition to "MV-style" cel-frame animations
. Otherwise the improvements are mostly just quality of life things like:
Manual layers for painting maps;
A list of map events by name;
No line limit for the Script command;
Improved user interfaces for plugin stuff (author URL, load order alerts, command arg types);
Built-in options for which MV needs plugins, e.g. splash, screen/tile size, time progress battle;
Custom character generator part X/Y offsets.

posts.author: freakytapir
posts.body:
Besides the raw eventing system, I think MZ has some great functions like a list of all events on a map and searchable events (Like all events containing a certain variable/switch/name).
The plugin comands being menu based is also a great function for me.
